Quickflver , called mercury by the chymists, is a naturally fluid mineral, and the heaviest of all known bodies next to gold, and is the more heavy and fluid, as it is more pure ; its nature is so homogene and limple, that it is a question whether gold itself be more so : it penetrates the parts of all the other metals, renders them brittle, and in part dissolves them : it is wholly volatile in the fire, and may be driven up in vapour by a degree of heat very little greater than that of boiling water : it is the least tenacious of all bodies, and every smaller drop may be again divided by the lightest touch into a multitude of others, and is the most divisible of all bodies : mercury very readily mixes with gold, silver, lead and tin, by chymical operations, but not without difficulty with copper and iron ;
